scope: Evidence-based phase0/phase1 software-stage observability under the explicitly recorded measurement boundaries
M1_acceptance_basis: Reproducible dual-VM configuration and two verified native CPU topologies.
Controlled synthetic SGI and verified Linux memory pressure with observed residency and lifecycle.
Consistent software T0-T6 event association, loss statistics and explicit selected-stage denominators.
Eight independent recorder on/off pairs quantify enabled recorder operations separately.
Coarse stage delays identify the main hundred-microsecond intervals while preserving clock/probe limits.
retained_boundaries: Nominal counter scale and calibration brackets; no absolute physical clock accuracy or future update-step bound.
T0 is Hypervisor visible; T4 is pre-backend software boundary; T6 is Guest thread completion.
Frequency and thermal measurements are quiescent snapshots, not continuous-window guarantees.
Firmware version text is observed; exact firmware binary identity is not established.
Recorder-operation increment does not isolate all timestamp, hook, mailbox, calibration or fence costs.
Cache event attribution, DSU and bandwidth control capability remain unverified conditional options.
New shared-core functional throughput includes handoff and an uncontended post-task tail.
remaining_phase2: Preregistered A/B intensity and controlled relative-phase sensitivity with an independently timed B exposure definition.
Validate any changed measurement path and quantify its recorder overhead before performance use.
Report scoped negative/inconclusive results if no stable interaction; do not enter phase3 or Joint without their evidence gates.
